problem: LoRaWAN does not use cluster heads. In LoRaWAN, end devices send to gateways, and gateways are transparent bridges to a network server; there is no cluster-head layer. A student may carry this wrong topology into an exam answer.
fix: Industry uses clustering ideas in industrial wireless mesh standards (WirelessHART, ISA100.11a) and in Zigbee cluster-tree topologies; LoRaWAN is a star-of-stars network with no cluster head.

problem: 'a 5× reduction' can be misread as 'reduced by 5 times' (a 500% cut). The bytes fall to one-fifth of the original, i.e. an 80% cut.
fix: Gateway inbound falls from 2,764,800 bytes/day to 552,960 bytes/day, one-fifth of the original (an 80% cut, 5 times fewer bytes); node-to-CH traffic still exists.

problem: Δt is called 'reporting interval' without saying whose. Node reporting interval and cluster-head reporting interval can differ, and the formula only counts head-to-gateway messages, so Δt must be the CH interval.
fix: Δt is the cluster head's reporting interval in seconds (the node-to-CH interval is separate).

problem: Each step label is doubled ('step 1: 1.'), which looks like a numbering slip when read on a phone.
fix: Use one label per step, for example 'Step 1: Reports per node per day = 86,400 ÷ 60 = 1,440.'
